questions.passage: In his essay "Of Smells," French philosopher Michel de Montaigne explores a relatively light subject, but he addresses heavier fare in "Of the Punishment of Cowardice." Regardless of subject matter, Montaigne works to question his own perspective throughout his essays. ______ his personal motto was "What do I know?"
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Montaigne questions his own perspective, so his motto "What do I know?" is fitting.

questions.passage: The World Cup of men's soccer, one of the biggest sporting events on the planet, brought 32 national teams from six continents to the host country, Brazil, in 2014. The event, which is held every four years, has expanded greatly since it was played in Italy in 1934. ______ the World Cup included only 16 teams, most from Europe and the Americas.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text contrasts 2014 with the 1934 tournament; "Then" moves back to that earlier time.

questions.passage: Cacti store water in their thick stems. ______ they can survive long periods without rain.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Surviving without rain is a result of storing water.

questions.passage: The first part of the hike follows a gentle, shaded path along the river. ______ the second part climbs steeply up a rocky, exposed ridge.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The two parts of the hike are opposites, so a contrast is needed.

questions.passage: Many birds migrate long distances each year. The Arctic tern, ______ travels from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back, the longest known migration of any animal.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The Arctic tern is an example of a bird that migrates long distances.

questions.passage: Modernista architects championed nature in their designs. ______ the dramatic archways and botanical glasswork of the Palau Mornau, a Modernista private home designed by Manuel Raspall, couldn't exactly grow in a forest; still, one sees natural influences in Raspall's penchant for curves (rather than right angles) and plant- and animal-inspired flourishes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The writer concedes that the Palau Mornau's features couldn't grow in a forest, then says "still" nature's influence shows. "Granted" signals the concession. Said's key had C, but "Thus" would mean the claim follows from the first sentence, which it doesn't.

questions.passage: In a 2005 study by Mellado et al., the researchers determined the ratio of three different plant subtypes within the diet of sheep: graminoids, forbs, and browse. ______ the researchers determined the relative quantities of the plants the animal consumed.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence restates the first in plainer words, so "That is" fits.

questions.passage: In Argentina, the Chamber of Deputies is elected via a proportional representation (PR) system. In PR elections, votes are cast (not for specific candidates, as they are in single-member plurality systems, but for political parties) and then tabulated; ______ each qualifying party is awarded a number of seats proportional to the number of votes it received.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Seats are awarded in proportion to the votes counted, so the result follows from the tally: "accordingly."

questions.passage: Before the first railroads were built in Australia, engineers warned against using multiple track widths across the continent. ______ regional officials couldn't agree on a single-width system. Thus, railways in Queensland, like the Durundur Railway, were made using narrow tracks, while those in Victoria were built with broad tracks.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Engineers warned against multiple widths, but officials still couldn't agree: "Nevertheless."

questions.passage: Joseph Goodrich was an outspoken abolitionist whose Wisconsin home was a stop on the Underground Railroad (the network of people and places that some enslaved people used to escape to freedom). ______ supporters of the railroad were secretive about their antislavery views. By and large, they were vocal abolitionists like Goodrich.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Only some supporters were secretive; "by and large" they were vocal. "Occasionally" marks the exception.

questions.passage: The work of contemporary Asian American poet John Yau often incorporates references to other poems and works of visual art. Typically, these allusive gestures are subtle, recognized by only the most attentive of Yau's readers. In his 2013 poem "Further Adventures in Monochrome," ______ Yau explicitly identifies a particular artwork—Yves Klein's 1960 painting *Silence is Golden*—as the poem's inspiration.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Yau's allusions are usually subtle, but in this poem he names the artwork outright, which is a contrast, so "however." (The choices in Said's copy were garbled, so we restored them.)

questions.passage: With some elements, like selenium, scientists were able to isolate a relatively pure sample of the substance shortly after discovering its existence—but this wasn't the case with all elements. ______ the isolation process took a few years. The element molybdenum, for instance, was discovered in 1778 but not isolated until 1781.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Not every element was isolated right away; "often" the process took years, and molybdenum is an example.

questions.passage: Firefly luciferase (Fluc) is a distinctly evolved enzyme that can oxidize a substrate called D-luciferin to induce bioluminescence and can act as a fatty acyl-CoA synthetase (ACS) enzyme, a class of enzyme present in all insects. ______ Fluc is a bifunctional enzyme whose presence indicates an insect is capable of emitting light. In contrast, the presence of ACS alone would be insufficient for determining bioluminescence.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The sentence restates the previous one more plainly (Fluc does two jobs, so it signals light-emitting ability): "That is."

questions.passage: A merchant's ledger from 1840 shows that he sold far more cotton cloth than silk. ______ silk accounted for most of his profits, since each bolt of it sold for many times the price of cotton.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Selling less silk yet earning most of his profit from it is a surprising contrast, so **Nevertheless** fits. *Accordingly* wrongly treats the profits as a result of selling more cotton.

questions.passage: Most stars in the night sky look white to the unaided eye. ______ stars vary considerably in color, from the deep red of cooler stars to the blue-white of the hottest ones, differences that become obvious in long-exposure photographs.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence corrects the impression given in the first, so **In reality** fits. *As a result* and *For this reason* wrongly suggest the colors are caused by stars looking white.

questions.passage: Behavioral economists have shown that people often stick with whatever option is selected by default. This tendency is not necessarily a sign of laziness or confusion, however. ______ people may reasonably treat a default as a recommendation from the experts who designed the choice.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: After saying what the tendency is not, the text offers a different explanation, so **Rather** fits. *Nevertheless* signals a contrast that is not there.

questions.passage: Space scientist Christine Chen is excited about the potential of the new James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Unlike its predecessor, the Hubble Telescope, the JWST is primarily an infrared telescope. Most light from distant galaxies is infrared; ______ the JWST can provide Chen and her team much more information about these galaxies than the Hubble could.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Because distant galaxies give off mostly infrared light, an infrared telescope can learn more: "consequently."

questions.passage: During many historic New York City parades, including the 1952 ticker-tape parade for US Olympic champions, the ribbonlike swirls descending on the scene were paper spools from "tickers," telegraph machines that were used to transmit stock prices. ______ the tickers had long since been retired by the time of the parade for the New York Mets in 1986. Then, shredded standard paper enriched the celebration.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: It is unsurprising that ticker machines had been retired by 1986; "Of course" signals this obvious point before "Then, shredded paper ..."

questions.passage: Sound loses energy much more slowly as it travels through water than as it travels through air. ______ the low calls of some whales can be heard by other whales hundreds of kilometers away.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Whales hearing each other far away is a result of sound losing energy slowly in water.

questions.passage: Many early jazz musicians learned to play by ear rather than by reading written music. ______ some of the era's best-known bandleaders read music fluently and wrote out detailed arrangements for their orchestras.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Bandleaders who read music fluently contrast with musicians who played by ear.

questions.passage: Building the new metro line required closing several busy streets for months. ______ the city ran free shuttle buses along the affected routes until construction was finished.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The free buses were the city's reaction to the street closures, so **In response** fits.

questions.passage: Analyses of Greenland ice cores in the 1980s suggested that the warming at the end of the Younger Dryas, a cold period about 12,900 to 11,700 years ago, unfolded over several centuries. Later cores sampled at much finer resolution, ______ allowed glaciologist Richard Alley and his colleagues to show that much of the warming occurred within just a few decades.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Early ice-core work suggested the shift was gradual; the newer, finer-resolution samples show it happened in a few decades. That is a contrast, so "however." (Said's file had only 26 questions in this module, so we added this one.)

questions.passage: Newer offshore wind turbines often outperform older models. For example, Denmark's Vindeby offshore wind farm, built in 1991, had wind turbines that generated about 0.5 megawatts (MW) of electricity each. ______ Denmark's Kriegers Flak offshore wind farm, built in 2021, has turbines that can generate about 8 MW of electricity each.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: A 1991 turbine made 0.5 MW; a 2021 one makes about 8 MW. The comparison contrasts them: "In contrast."

questions.passage: Ecologists like David N.M. Mbora use trophic pyramids to illustrate the food chain within a given ecosystem. At a typical pyramid's base are primary producers, like plants, followed by herbivores at the second trophic level, then omnivores and carnivores at the third. ______ at the fourth, highest trophic level are apex predators, like tigers, that feed on the animals below.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text walks up the pyramid level by level; the fourth, highest level comes "Lastly."

questions.passage: In a 2022 analysis of 200 terms, researchers found a broad pattern of valence-dependent mutation in which negative adjectives saw a faster rate of cognate replacement—the rate at which a word will be replaced over time with a noncognate form—than other words. ______ the adjective "illegal" would be expected to mutate faster than the noun "debt."
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Negative adjectives change faster, so it follows that "illegal" should mutate faster than "debt": "Thus."

questions.passage: In the early 1970s, Albert Popa took up graffiti art, spraying his work onto what was at the time an unconventional surface: concrete. ______ Albert's son David has chosen an unusual canvas for his new art project, *Fractured*. In this remarkable work, the artist draws charcoal faces onto fragmented ice floes in Finland, creating the visual effect of a face slowly fracturing.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Albert chose an unusual surface (concrete); his son David also chose an unusual canvas (ice): "Likewise."

questions.passage: Winter wheat must go through a period of cold weather before it can produce grain. ______ farmers in Kansas plant it in autumn, so that the young plants pass the winter in the fields and are ready to harvest in early summer.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Farmers plant in autumn *because* the wheat needs cold weather, so **For this reason** fits.

questions.passage: A camera can record a whole landscape in a fraction of a second. ______ a painter might spend weeks or even months on a single landscape.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The painter's weeks are set against the camera's fraction of a second, so the sentences are being compared and contrasted.

questions.passage: Archaeologists usually dig with small hand tools, removing soil only a few centimeters at a time. ______ they record the exact position of every object before lifting it out of the ground.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Recording each object's position is another careful practice added to digging slowly, so **In addition** fits.

questions.passage: The world's first airplane, the 1903 Wright Flyer, was not very aerodynamic, as evidenced by its low lift-to-drag ratio of just 3:1. The F-4 Phantom II jet, like most modern aircraft, is far more aerodynamic. ______ its lift-to-drag ratio is more than twice that of the Wright Flyer.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The ratio comparison gives a precise detail about how much more aerodynamic the F-4 is: "Specifically."

questions.passage: Modernist architects championed nature in their designs. ______ the domed rooftop and painted floral designs of Casa Estapa, a Modernista private home designed by Bernardi Martorell i Rius, couldn't exactly grow in a forest. Still, one sees natural influences in Martorell i Rius's penchant for curves (rather than right angles) and plant- and animal-inspired flourishes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The writer concedes that the house's features couldn't grow in a forest before saying "Still," nature shows. "Of course" signals that concession.

questions.passage: Before the first railroads were built in Australia, engineers warned against using multiple track widths across the continent. ______ regional officials couldn't agree on a single-width system. Thus, railways in Victoria, like the Victorian Goldfields Railway, were made using wide tracks, while those in New South Wales were built with narrow tracks.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Engineers warned against multiple widths, but officials still couldn't agree: "Nevertheless."

questions.passage: Legislators in Botswana are elected via a first-past-the-post electoral system. In the winner-take-all voting system, the seat is awarded to the candidate who receives not a majority but a plurality (i.e., greatest number) of votes. ______ if several popular candidates are vying for the same seat, it is possible for a candidate to win an election despite receiving less than 50% of the votes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Because seats go to a plurality, it follows that a winner can get under 50%: "Accordingly."

questions.passage: Large volcanic eruptions can send sulfur dioxide high into the atmosphere, where it forms tiny droplets that reflect sunlight back into space. ______ a major eruption is sometimes followed by a year or two of slightly cooler temperatures around the world.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Cooler temperatures are a result of the droplets reflecting sunlight, so **Consequently** fits.

questions.passage: Most animated films of the 1930s were made from drawings, with each frame drawn and painted by hand. Stop-motion animators, ______ built small physical models and photographed them, moving each figure slightly between shots.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Stop-motion used models instead of drawings, which contrasts with the method in the first sentence.

questions.passage: When a supermarket chain installed self-checkout machines, analysts predicted that it would sharply cut its workforce. The number of cashier positions at the chain did decline. ______ total employment at its stores held steady, because many workers who had once operated registers moved into jobs restocking shelves, helping customers, and preparing online orders.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text grants that cashier jobs fell, then says total jobs held steady anyway, so a concession like **Even so** is needed. *Accordingly* would wrongly present steady employment as a result of the decline.

questions.passage: Desert locusts usually live alone and avoid one another. ______ when heavy rains bring many of them together, they change color and behavior and begin to form huge swarms.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Forming swarms is the opposite of living alone, so a contrast word is needed.

questions.passage: Apprenticeship programs let workers earn wages while they learn a trade. ______ the programs give employers a chance to train workers in the specific skills their businesses need.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another benefit of apprenticeships, so **In addition** fits.

questions.passage: Engineers in earthquake-prone regions design buildings to sway slightly during an earthquake rather than resist the shaking rigidly, since rigid structures are more likely to crack. ______ many tall buildings in these regions rest on flexible bearings that absorb some of the ground's motion.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Flexible bearings follow from the goal of letting buildings sway, so the second sentence is a result of the first.

questions.passage: Through the late nineteenth century, most geologists were convinced that the continents had always been fixed in place. ______ when the idea that continents slowly drift across Earth's surface was proposed in the early twentieth century, it was widely rejected.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The rejection follows from geologists' belief in fixed continents, so a cause-and-effect word like **Accordingly** fits. *Nevertheless* would suggest the idea was rejected despite that belief.

questions.passage: Director Federico Russo rarely used music in his films, believing that a musical score told audiences how to feel. His final film is no exception: it has no score at all. ______ the film is far from quiet; Russo filled its soundtrack with the hum of traffic, distant radios, and the calls of street vendors.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Having no score might suggest a quiet film, but the film is full of sound, so a contrast word like **Still** is needed. *In other words* would wrongly present "far from quiet" as a restatement of "no score."

questions.passage: Economists generally expect workers to quit their jobs more often when unemployment is low, since new jobs are then easy to find. Two decades of data from one region's labor market fit this pattern closely. ______ in the region's tourism industry, quit rates stayed high even in years of high unemployment, because many tourism jobs are seasonal and workers routinely change employers between seasons.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Tourism is an exception to the pattern just described, so a contrast is needed. *For instance* would wrongly present tourism as an example of the pattern.

questions.passage: In 1949, Frank Zamboni developed an ice rink resurfacing machine. As Zamboni's machine moved along the rink's surface, it first scraped off the top layer of ice. ______ it sprayed water into the deep grooves left behind by customers' skates. Lastly, it smoothed over the newly formed ice.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The steps go in order: first scraped, "Next" sprayed, "Lastly" smoothed.

questions.passage: Wool traps air between its fibers, which helps keep heat close to the body. ______ wool has been one of the most common materials for winter clothing for thousands of years.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Wool's warmth is the reason it is used for winter clothing, so a cause-and-effect transition fits.

questions.passage: Most robots in factories repeat a single motion thousands of times a day. ______ robots used in hospitals must handle a wide variety of tasks, from delivering medicine to guiding visitors through hallways.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Hospital robots do many different tasks, the opposite of factory robots that repeat one motion.

questions.passage: The illustrator begins every page with a light pencil sketch. ______ she adds watercolor, layering pale washes before painting the darker details.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Adding color is the step that follows the sketch, so a sequence word fits.

questions.passage: According to Duverger's law, countries with single-ballot majoritarian elections for single-member districts tend to polarize into two-party systems, wherein dueling political parties consistently dominate the political system. ______ countries with proportional-representation electoral systems tend to support multi-partyism, under which power gets distributed among many political parties.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Majoritarian systems lead to two parties; proportional systems do the opposite: "Conversely."

questions.passage: The Tommy Atkins mango is the most widely grown mango variety in Brazil, one of the world's leading mango producers. ______ in 2018, 1.4 million metric tons of mangoes were produced.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: "There" refers back to Brazil, where the mangoes were produced.

questions.passage: In retrospect, one of the lessons of the 2003 Human Genome Project is that a gene is affected by many factors, not the least of which is its interactions with the protein products of other genes. ______ rather than just focusing on the human genome, efforts to better understand gene mutations related to disease have begun to consider the human proteome, the complete set of proteins expressed by human genes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Because genes are shaped by interactions with proteins, researchers have begun studying the proteome: "Accordingly."

questions.passage: In a 1984 study by Warren et al., the researchers determined the ratio of three different plant subtypes within the diet of sheep: graminoids, forbs, and browse. ______ the researchers determined the relative quantities of the plants the animal consumed.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence restates the first in plainer terms: "That is."

questions.passage: Many endurance athletes train at high altitude, where the air contains less oxygen. Their bodies respond by producing more red blood cells, which carry oxygen to the muscles. ______ when these athletes return to lower elevations, their muscles can receive more oxygen than before.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Extra oxygen reaching the muscles is a result of the extra red blood cells, so **As a result** fits.

questions.passage: Most playwrights finish their scripts before rehearsals begin. The members of the Lanterna Theater Collective, ______ build their plays during rehearsals, improvising scenes together and writing down only the moments that work.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The collective works differently from most playwrights, so a contrast is needed: **by contrast**.

questions.passage: The noise of wind turbines is often cited as a reason that people oppose new wind farms. In one survey near a wind farm, however, residents who could see the turbines from their homes reported being bothered by the noise far more often than residents who heard the same noise levels but could not see the turbines. ______ the residents' annoyance may have had as much to do with the turbines' appearance as with their sound.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The last sentence is a conclusion drawn from the survey result, so **Hence** fits. *Even so* would wrongly signal a point that goes against the survey.

questions.passage: The body's internal clock is strongly influenced by light. ______ looking at bright screens late at night can make it harder to fall asleep.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Trouble falling asleep after screen light is a consequence of the clock's sensitivity to light, so **For this reason** fits.

questions.passage: Hydroelectric dams can produce electricity steadily, day and night. ______ they can flood large areas of land and block fish from moving up and down rivers.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: An advantage is followed by drawbacks, so a contrast is needed: **However**.

questions.passage: Pato, a traditional horseback game played in Argentina, requires riders to scoop a ball with leather handles off the ground while galloping at full speed. ______ riders must keep hold of the ball while opponents try to pull it away.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another demand of the game, so **In addition** fits.

questions.passage: Bar-headed geese migrate over the Himalayas, where oxygen at high altitudes is scarce. Their blood carries a form of hemoglobin that binds oxygen unusually well, and their lungs are large for birds of their size. ______ the geese usually follow lower valleys when they can, climbing to great heights only when the mountains force them to.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The geese are well equipped for high altitude, yet they avoid it when possible. That unexpected contrast calls for **Even so**. *As a result* wrongly suggests their adaptations cause them to stay low.

questions.passage: Many athletes believe that ice baths after exercise speed up muscle recovery, and some studies support this belief, finding that athletes report less soreness after sitting in cold water. ______ other studies suggest that taking ice baths regularly may reduce the muscle growth that strength training is meant to produce.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds a drawback that qualifies the benefit just described, so **At the same time** fits. *For instance* and *In short* would present the drawback as an example or summary of the benefit.

questions.passage: In most plays, the audience learns important information at the same moment the characters do. In Helen Ward's *The Locked Room*, ______ the audience learns in the first scene that the missing letter is hidden inside the piano, while the characters spend the rest of the play searching for it.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Ward's play does the opposite of most plays, so **by contrast** fits. *For example* would wrongly present it as a typical case.

questions.passage: Parchment, which was made from animal skin, was costly in medieval Europe. ______ scribes sometimes scraped the old writing off used sheets so that they could write on them again.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Reusing sheets is a result of parchment being expensive, so a cause-and-effect transition fits.

questions.passage: Most of a cell's DNA is found in its nucleus. ______ a small amount is located in the mitochondria, the structures that supply the cell with energy, and this DNA is passed down almost entirely from mothers.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence names an exception to the first (DNA outside the nucleus), so a contrast is needed.

questions.passage: Ecologists predicted that removing an old dam would at first harm fish downstream, since years of trapped sediment would suddenly wash through the river. Fish numbers below the former dam did fall sharply in the first year. ______ by the third year, they had climbed well above any level recorded while the dam stood.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The recovery contrasts with the first-year drop, so **Nevertheless** fits. *Indeed* would wrongly present the recovery as more evidence of the predicted harm.

questions.passage: Some genetic traits are controlled by a single gene. Most traits, ______ such as height, are shaped by many genes working together.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Traits shaped by many genes contrast with traits controlled by one gene.

questions.passage: Many early printed books were bound between heavy wooden boards covered with leather. ______ some of them weighed several kilograms and had to be read on a table or a stand.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Being too heavy to hold is a result of the heavy wooden bindings.

questions.passage: Wetlands provide food and shelter for many kinds of animals. ______ they filter pollutants from the water that flows through them, helping to keep nearby rivers clean.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Filtering water is a second, separate benefit of wetlands, so **In addition** fits.

questions.passage: Psychologists have long known that people forget much of what they learn within days. More surprising is how much remains: in one study, adults who had studied a language in school decades earlier still recognized hundreds of its words. ______ the rapid forgetting that follows learning appears to level off, leaving a stable core of knowledge that can last a lifetime.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The last sentence restates the point of the study in general terms, so **In other words** fits. It is a summary, not another example.

questions.passage: Bookbinders of the 1500s often cut up old manuscripts and used the scraps to strengthen the spines of new books, regarding the scraps as worthless. ______ these hidden fragments now preserve passages of texts that survive nowhere else, and modern scholars prize them.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Material treated as worthless turned out to be precious, an outcome opposite to what was expected. That is **Ironically**. *Accordingly* would wrongly make the scraps' value a result of their being thought worthless.

questions.passage: Plant breeders had assumed that tomatoes bred for larger fruit would lose flavor, since bigger fruits tend to contain more water. ______ several large-fruited varieties in a recent taste test were rated as flavorful as smaller traditional types.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The taste test went against the breeders' assumption, so a contrast word is needed.

questions.passage: Many shoppers say they compare prices carefully before buying groceries. ______ in one study, fewer than half of the shoppers leaving a supermarket could correctly recall the price of an item they had placed in their carts only minutes earlier.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The study contrasts with what shoppers say about themselves, so **However** fits.

questions.passage: Samuel Morse and Alfred Vail designed their telegraph code so that the letters used most often in English would take the least time to send. The letter *E*, ______ is represented by a single dot, while a rarely used letter such as *Q* requires four signals.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: *E* is a specific case of the design rule in the first sentence, so **for example** fits.

questions.passage: In a book code, each word of a message is replaced by numbers showing where that word appears in a particular book—page 112, line 4, word 6, for instance. Such codes can be extremely hard to break: without the right book, a code breaker has almost nothing to work with. ______ they have a serious weakness. Once an enemy learns which book is being used, every message sent with it can be read.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text moves from the code's strength to a weakness that exists despite it, so **Even so** fits. *Therefore* wrongly presents the weakness as a result of the strength.

questions.passage: Many marine mammals are protected from cold water by a thick layer of fat called blubber. ______ the blubber of a bowhead whale, which lives in Arctic waters, can be about half a meter thick.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The bowhead whale is an example of a marine mammal with thick blubber, so **For example** fits.

questions.passage: Many plants in hot climates open the tiny pores in their leaves during the day to take in carbon dioxide. Cacti, ______ open their pores only at night, when cooler air means they lose less water.

questions.passage: Elephants have excellent memories. ______ they can remember the locations of water sources they visited years before.

questions.passage: The team expected the experiment to take one week. ______ problems with the equipment meant that it took nearly a month.

questions.passage: The plant's leaves were turning yellow, and its growth had slowed. ______ the gardener moved it to a sunnier spot and began watering it less often.

questions.passage: Many early critics dismissed photography as a mechanical process that required no artistic skill. ______ some of the same critics later praised photographers whose careful choices of light and composition produced images as expressive as paintings.

questions.passage: Volcanic eruptions can cool the planet for a year or two by sending fine particles high into the atmosphere, where they reflect sunlight. ______ the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines lowered average global temperatures by about half a degree Celsius over the following year.

questions.passage: The weather forecast called for heavy rain on Saturday. ______ the school moved its outdoor sports day to the following week.

questions.passage: The team's first robot design was too heavy to climb the ramp. ______ the engineers replaced its steel frame with one made of aluminum.

questions.passage: The new medicine worked well in laboratory tests on cells. ______ in early trials with patients, it caused side effects so serious that researchers stopped testing it.

questions.passage: The museum's collection of fossils is very large. ______ it includes more than two thousand dinosaur bones.

questions.passage: To make paper by hand, workers first soak plant fibers in water until they break down into pulp. ______ they spread a thin layer of the pulp across a screen and let it dry into a sheet.

questions.passage: In a given rock formation, Rhaetian rock from 208.5 million years ago might directly abut Lochkovian rock from 419.2 million years ago, with millions of years of material missing in between. ______ time did not stand still during these intervening years; the unaccounted-for sedimentary material was likely removed from the stratigraphic record via erosion and weathering.

questions.passage: When it was built in the nineteenth century, the Eiffel Tower was criticized—even protested—for its unique appearance. ______ the spire-like structure earned not just acceptance but adoration, and its iconic design is now echoed in everything from the Eiffel Tower replica in Klagenfurt, Austria, to the Tokyo Tower in Tokyo, Japan.

questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says honeybee colonies were long assumed to be ruled by the queen. The second gives the opposite view: workers, not the queen, make the key decisions. "In reality" introduces the truth that corrects the assumption.

questions.passage: For millennia, acorns were a staple food for the Tongva people, the Indigenous inhabitants of what is now the Los Angeles basin. questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Raw acorns are very bitter, so it was necessary to process them. "Therefore" signals this consequence.

questions.passage: Rocket Geyser, found in Yellowstone National Park, is a cone geyser, a type of geyser that forms a mound of silica around the narrow geyser vent as volcanic rock dissolved in the water is deposited during eruptions. ______ Yellowstone's fountain geysers, such as Jewel Geyser, erupt from larger openings where water collects in a pool.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

questions.passage: In ArtMed inSight, a series of art-based medical education classes taught by Anne Willieme, medical students learn to use techniques more often associated with the arts, such as slowing down interpretation and considering multiple perspectives. ______ Willieme's students develop better observational skills, enhancing their ability to understand and diagnose patients effectively.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Students learn artistic techniques, and through doing that they develop better observation skills. "In doing so" links the activity to its result.

questions.passage: The World Cup of men's soccer, one of the biggest sporting events on the planet, brought 32 national teams from six continents to the host country, Russia, in 2018. ______ only 16 teams, all from Europe and the Americas, competed in the 1962 World Cup in Chile.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text compares the 2018 World Cup (32 teams from six continents) with the 1962 one (16 teams from two regions). "In comparison" introduces this contrast.

questions.passage: Developed by Les Paul in 1945, multitrack recording allows music producers to record songs by layering separate musical tracks on top of one another. For example, producers can first record the drums. ______ they can record the guitars on top of the drums. questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

questions.passage: Nineteenth-century Modernista architects championed nature in their designs. Granted, the wavy stone façade and ornate floral tilework of Casa Batlló, a Modernista private home designed by Antoni Gaudí, couldn't exactly grow in a forest. ______ one sees natural influences in Gaudí's penchant for curves (rather than right angles) and plant- and animal-inspired flourishes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text admits that Casa Batlló's stone and tiles could not literally grow in a forest, but still one can see nature's influence. "Still" marks this concession.

questions.passage: Early telescopes produced blurry images with colored fringes because their lenses bent different colors of light by different amounts. questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Because Newton believed lenses could not solve the problem, he used a mirror instead. "Accordingly" signals an action taken in response to that conclusion.

questions.passage: Ancient Rome's concrete has survived for two thousand years, while much modern concrete cracks within decades. questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The last sentence restates the process just described (lime sealing cracks) in simpler terms: the concrete repaired itself. "In other words" signals a restatement.

questions.passage: Some economists predicted that the spread of ATMs in the 1980s would eliminate most jobs for bank tellers. ______ the number of tellers in the United States actually grew in the following decades, as banks used the savings from ATMs to open more branches.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

questions.passage: Glass frogs, found in Central and South American rain forests, have transparent skin on their undersides, so observers can see their hearts and other organs. ______ when the frogs sleep, they can store most of their red blood cells in their livers, making their bodies even harder to see against the leaves.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another remarkable feature that also makes the frogs hard to see. *Moreover* adds information that builds on the first point.

questions.passage: Early bicycles of the 1870s had a very large front wheel and a small rear wheel, which made them difficult and dangerous to ride. ______ the "safety bicycle," introduced in the 1880s, had two wheels of similar size and a chain that drove the rear wheel, making it far easier to balance.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The safety bicycle's equal wheels differ from the earlier design's mismatched wheels, and it was safer. *By contrast* signals that difference.

questions.passage: Karel Čapek's 1920 play *R.U.R. Beyond the simple coining of a term,
Despite its creation of such an iconic trope,
Ultimately limited in its lasting influence,

questions.passage: Most spiders spin webs and wait for insects to become trapped in them. ______ jumping spiders hunt actively, stalking their prey and leaping onto it from a distance.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Waiting in a web contrasts with actively stalking and leaping, so *However* fits.

questions.passage: To make a bowl on a potter's wheel, a potter first presses a lump of wet clay into the center of the spinning wheel. ______ the potter pushes a thumb into the middle of the clay to open it and slowly pulls up the walls.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text describes steps in order: first center the clay, then open it and pull up the walls. *Next* signals the following step.

questions.passage: For centuries, Europeans used the phrase "black swan" to describe something impossible, since every swan they had ever seen was white. ______ in 1697, Dutch explorers led by Willem de Vlamingh saw black swans in western Australia, and the phrase came to mean an unexpected event that overturns what people thought they knew.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says black swans were thought impossible; the second reports their discovery. *However* signals this contradiction.

questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Water behaves the opposite way from most substances, so *by contrast* fits. Water is not an example of the general pattern (A); it is an exception.

questions.passage: Some species of bamboo can grow almost a meter taller in a single day, faster than nearly any other plant. ______ a bamboo grove can be harvested again just a few years after it is cut, making bamboo a quickly renewable building material.

questions.passage: It's tempting to think that the comic strips *Jump Start* and *Wee Pals* have the same main purpose—to amuse—because both feature humorous situations. ______ *Wee Pals* focuses just as much on challenging readers with sociopolitical commentary as it does on making them laugh.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The first sentence describes a tempting but mistaken assumption; the second gives the truth that corrects it. *In reality* signals that correction.

questions.passage: The Inca Empire, which stretched along the Andes Mountains of South America, had no system of writing as Europeans understood it. ______ Inca officials recorded information such as population counts and tax records using quipus: bundles of cords tied with knots of different types and in different positions.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The Inca had no writing, so they used knotted cords in its place. *Instead* signals that alternative.

questions.passage: Some animals survive the winter by hibernating. ______ many bears sleep in dens for months, living off fat they stored during the summer and fall.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Bears sleeping through the winter is an example of hibernating, so *For example* fits.

questions.passage: The team practiced for two hours every day for a month before the tournament. ______ the players were well prepared and won the regional championship.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Winning followed from all the practice, so *As a result* signals cause and effect.

questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence corrects the popular image in the first, so *In truth* fits. *Accordingly* would wrongly suggest the second idea follows from the first.

questions.passage: Luminița Ilinca Ignat is a space scientist who works on the James Webb Space Telescope, or JWST. questions.explanation: The first sentence stresses how little the violin has changed; the second adds a qualification (they aren't identical). *That said* introduces such a qualification.
